paragraphs: Symbium runs an instant permitting service that lets homeowners and contractors see what a property allows, scope a project such as solar panels or a heat pump, and then file and manage the permit application. The company is based in San Francisco and puts its initial focus on permitting for residential decarbonization projects.

Compliance checks run against the applicable building, zoning, and energy codes while the applicant is still scoping the work. The technology underneath, called Complaw, is described as a TurboTax-like mechanization of regulatory analysis first built by the founding team at Stanford AI Lab. It layers onto the permitting workflows a building department already has, with contractors getting issuance within seconds of applying.

Contractors use it to accelerate permit issuance across a range of project types. The company says it has saved contractors and city staff time, and puts the running total at 3,500,000 project hours so far. It names Elemental Impact, Third Derivative, Uptake Alliance, and IMPEL among its backers. It was founded by Leila Banijamali, Abhijeet Mohapatra and Michael Genesereth during work at Stanford University. Recognition it lists includes a California Building Officials industry achievement award and a United States Conference of Mayors Civic Challenge.

quote.text: Symbium performs compliance checks against applicable building, zoning, and energy codes as a permit applicant is scoping out a project.
